# Decomposition handoff: Running club

Source vision: `plans/vision/running-club.md` (status: ready, created 2026-10-01)
Produced by: vision-decomposer, background task t1, 2026-10-06
State: **decomposition done; no stubs created yet; waiting for the owner's OK at the decomposition checkpoint**

This file is a handoff note, not a plan. It is not under `plans/functional/`, so `listStubs`
will not pick it up. The stubs are created by the library, run by the session (see "Session actions").

---

## What was read, and what could not be done

- **Vision:** read in full.
- **Canvas:** none. Glob `plans/canvas/*` in the project root matched 0 files, so goals come from the vision alone.
- **Other plans:** none. Glob `plans/**/*` matched 1 file (the vision), so there are no functional,
  implementation or todo plans that could overlap.
- **Library:** `src/lib/vision-decomposer.js` is not in this project. Glob `src/lib/*.js` matched 0 files,
  and reading `<the CTOC repository>` was refused (no permission). So I could not check the exact
  signatures of `validateVisionReadiness`, `createStub` or `decomposeVision`. The calls below follow
  the documented signatures and are marked as unverified.
- **No stubs were written.** Only the library creates stubs, and this agent cannot run JavaScript.
  I did not write stub files by hand.

## Readiness gate (checked by hand; the library has not given its verdict)

| Check | Kind | Result | Evidence in the vision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Problem statement present | blocking | pass | `### Problem`: schedule lost in the chat thread; spreadsheets that people stop updating |
| Target audience present | blocking | pass | `### Target audience`: one club of about 200 runners, using phones; run leaders |
| Success criteria present | blocking | pass | `### Success criteria`: 4 numbered, measurable criteria |
| Scope and boundaries defined | warning | pass | `### Scope`: an In list and an Out list |
| `type: vision` marker | warning | pass | `type: vision` in the frontmatter, plus a `## Vision:` heading |

Judgement on whether it is specific enough to decompose: yes. Every criterion has a number, a
time limit or a percentage, and an actor.

The four success criteria are numbered below as they are in the vision:
- **SC1:** a member finds this week's group runs, with place and start time, in under 30 seconds.
- **SC2:** at least half of the members who attend a group run, as counted by its run leader, signed up beforehand.
- **SC3:** a member logs a run in under 20 seconds and sees their distance for the month.
- **SC4:** at least 60% of active members (those who came to at least one group run that month) log a run that month.

---

## Goals

### Goal 1: Find and sign up for group runs
- **Actor:** club member (main actor); run leader (the member who posts a run and counts who came)
- **Impact:** members look up the week's runs in one place and sign up before they come, instead of
  scrolling the chat thread. Run leaders post runs there and record who came.
- **Success metric:** SC1 and SC2.

### Goal 2: Keep my monthly distance
- **Actor:** club member
- **Impact:** members log each run in the club's place right after running and see their distance for
  the month. They keep doing it every month, instead of using a spreadsheet they give up on.
- **Success metric:** SC3 and SC4. SC4 defines "active member" through group-run attendance, so it is
  *measured* using attendance data from Goal 1. That is a dependency of the metric, not of the build.

Why two goals: the vision's own one-sentence summary has two halves ("find and sign up for group runs" /
"keep their own monthly distance"). Each half has its own criteria (SC1+SC2 / SC3+SC4) and its own
change in behaviour. Run leaders stay inside Goal 1 because a goal for members alone would have nothing
to show until leaders post runs.

---

## Stub 1: Find and sign up for group runs

*(This section goes word for word under the `## Decomposition` heading of stub 1.)*

**Goal:** members find the next seven days' group runs and sign up before they come; run leaders post the runs and record who came.
**Actor:** member (main); run leader (the member who posts the run). **Impact:** the run list and its sign-ups take the place of the chat thread.
**Success metric:** SC1 (find a run's place and start time in under 30 seconds), SC2 (at least 50% of recorded attendees signed up before the start time).

### Activities (backbone, in order of the user journey)
1. Post the week's runs (run leader)
2. Find and sign up for a run (member)
3. Count who came (run leader)

### Activity 1: Post the week's runs

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] **G1-S1 [MVP] Sign in from the chat link and post a run.** As a run leader, I want to open the club's link from the chat, sign in with my email, and post a group run with its day, start time and place, so that members find it in one place instead of in the chat thread.
  - Acceptance:
    - The first time a member opens the link, they enter their email and name, tap the sign-in link sent to that email, and arrive signed in. When they open the link again on the same phone, they are not asked to sign in again.
    - A signed-in member posts a run with a date, a start time and a place (free text, for example "Vondelpark, main entrance"). The run then appears in the club's run list with its day, start time, place and the poster's name as run leader.
    - If the date, start time or place is missing, the post is refused with a message that names the missing field. A date in the past is refused.
    - Someone who is not signed in sees the sign-in screen, not the run list.
  - Carries the shared sign-in. Stub 2 depends on this story for sign-in only.
  - Depends on: none.
  - INVEST: I pass, N pass, V pass, E pass, **S at the upper limit** (about 3 days: sign-in plus posting), T pass. If the Product Owner estimates more than 3 days, sign-in cannot be split off as a story of its own without leaving it with no user value. In that case, cut the posting part down to the three fields only.

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **G1-S2 Edit or cancel a run I posted.** As a run leader, I want to change the time or place of a run I posted, or cancel it, so that members do not turn up at the wrong place or for a run that is off.
  - Acceptance:
    - Only the member who posted a run sees Edit and Cancel on it.
    - After an edit, the list shows the new start time or place.
    - A cancelled run stays in the list marked "Cancelled", and no one can sign up for it.
  - Depends on: G1-S1.
  - INVEST: all pass. Independence note: the check "no one can sign up for a cancelled run" can only be tested once G1-S5 exists. If this story is built before G1-S5, that check moves into G1-S5's acceptance.
- [ ] **G1-S3 Repost a weekly run for next week.** As a run leader, I want to repost one of my runs for the same weekday next week in one action, so that I do not type the same run again every week.
  - Acceptance:
    - "Repeat next week" on a run I posted creates a run exactly 7 days later with the same start time and place, and it appears in the list.
    - It is refused, with the message "already posted", when I already have a run on that day at that time.
    - Sign-ups and attendance are not copied to the new run.
  - Depends on: G1-S1. INVEST: all pass.

### Activity 2: Find and sign up for a run

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] **G1-S5 [MVP] Sign up for a run, or withdraw.** As a member, I want to sign up for a run in the list and withdraw if my plans change, so that the run leader knows who to expect.
  - Acceptance:
    - On a run that has not started yet, a signed-in member taps "Sign up". The run then shows "You're going" to that member, and the count of members signed up goes up by 1.
    - "Withdraw" reverses it, and the count goes down by 1.
    - Signing up and withdrawing are closed once the run's start time has passed.
    - A member cannot be signed up twice for the same run.
    - The run leader sees the names of the members who signed up for their run.
    - Every sign-up stores the time it was made, so that "signed up beforehand" (before the start time) can be measured for SC2.
  - Depends on: G1-S1. INVEST: all pass.

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **G1-S4 Find this week's runs in under 30 seconds.** As a member, I want the club link to open straight on the runs of the next seven days, grouped by day with place and start time, so that I see where and when to run in under 30 seconds.
  - Acceptance:
    - When a signed-in member taps the club link in the chat, they land directly on the runs from today through the next 6 days, grouped by weekday with the earliest first. Each run shows its start time, place and run leader. Runs whose start time has passed are not shown.
    - No tap is needed after opening the link. The list reads on a 360 px-wide phone screen without zooming or sideways scrolling.
    - If no runs are posted for that period, the screen says "No group runs posted for the next 7 days".
    - SC1 check, timed with real people: 5 signed-in club members are each asked "where and when does Thursday's run start?". Each answers in under 30 s from tapping the chat link.
  - Depends on: G1-S1. INVEST: all pass.
  - Note: the thinnest end-to-end path uses G1-S1's basic list to find a run. SC1 is only shown to be met once this story exists.

### Activity 3: Count who came

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] **G1-S6 [MVP] Record who came.** As a run leader, I want to record which members came to my run by picking their names from the club's member list, so that the club knows the real attendance of every run.
  - Acceptance:
    - From the run's start time onward, the member who posted the run can open "Who came" and search members by name. For example, typing "jan" lists every member whose name contains "jan". The leader ticks each member who came, and the run then shows "N came".
    - The run leader can add or remove ticks at any later time, and the count updates.
    - Only the run's leader can record attendance. Other members see only the count.
    - Attendance is stored per member per run, not only as a number. This lets SC2 (attendees who signed up beforehand) and SC4 (active members) be computed.
  - Depends on: G1-S1. INVEST: all pass.

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **G1-S7 Count who came, starting from the sign-up list.** As a run leader, I want "Who came" to show the members who signed up first, each ticked with one tap, so that counting a group of 15 takes seconds instead of searching for every name.
  - Acceptance:
    - "Who came" shows the members who signed up at the top, each with a one-tap tick. Members who came without signing up are still added by search (G1-S6).
    - Worked example: a run has 12 sign-ups, 10 of them come, and 3 more members come without signing up. After 10 taps and 3 searches the run shows "13 came", and 10 of the 13 are marked as signed up beforehand.
  - Depends on: G1-S5, G1-S6. INVEST: all pass.

### Dependency order (stub 1)
1. G1-S1 (no dependencies)
2. G1-S2, G1-S3, G1-S4, G1-S5, G1-S6 (each depends on G1-S1 only)
3. G1-S7 (depends on G1-S5 and G1-S6)

**Thinnest end-to-end path:** G1-S1 → G1-S5 → G1-S6. A leader posts, a member signs up, and the leader records who came.

## Stub 2: Keep my monthly distance

*(This section goes word for word under the `## Decomposition` heading of stub 2.)*

**Goal:** members keep their distance for the month up to date in the club's place instead of in a spreadsheet they give up on.
**Actor:** member. **Impact:** members log each run right after running and see their total for the month, every month.
**Success metric:** SC3 (log a run in under 20 seconds and see the month's distance), SC4 (at least 60% of active members log at least one run that month; "active" = recorded by a run leader as present at one or more group runs that month, which uses G1-S6's data).

### Activities (backbone, in order of the user journey)
1. Log a run
2. See my monthly distance

### Activity 1: Log a run

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] **G2-S1 [MVP] Log a run and see my month's distance.** As a member, I want to log a run's distance and date and see my distance for this month straight away, so that I keep my total without a spreadsheet.
  - Acceptance:
    - "Log a run" asks for the distance in km (decimals allowed, for example 8.5) and the date, which defaults to today. Then Save.
    - After saving, the screen shows "This month: X km" including the new run. For example, 12.0 km already logged plus 8.5 shows "20.5 km".
    - 0, negative numbers and non-numbers are refused. A date in the future is refused. A past date is accepted and counts towards the month it falls in.
    - Logged runs are visible only to the member who logged them.
    - SC3 check, timed with real people: 5 signed-in members each log a given distance run today, starting from the chat link, in under 20 s, and read out their total for the month.
  - Depends on: **G1-S1 (sign-in). This is the only dependency between the two goals.**
  - INVEST: all pass.

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **G2-S2 Fix or delete a run I logged.** As a member, I want to correct the distance or date of a run I logged, or delete it, so that my monthly total stays right after a typo.
  - Acceptance:
    - A list of my logged runs (newest first) has Edit and Delete on each run. Delete asks for confirmation first.
    - Month totals update. For example, correcting 85 to 8.5 lowers that month's total by 76.5.
    - Changing a run's date to another month moves its distance to that month's total.
  - Depends on: G2-S1. INVEST: all pass.

### Activity 2: See my monthly distance

**Walking Skeleton:**
- [ ] **G2-S3 [MVP] See this month's distance at any time.** As a member, I want to see how far I have run this month without logging anything, so that I can check where I stand.
  - Acceptance:
    - "My distance" shows this month's total and the number of runs logged this month.
    - A month is a calendar month in the club's time zone. On the 1st of the month the total starts again at 0.
    - With no runs this month, it shows "0 km this month" and a "Log a run" button.
  - Depends on: G2-S1.
  - INVEST: all pass. **Small at the lower limit** (about half a day to a day). Merge it into G2-S4 if the Product Owner estimates it below half a day.

**Additional Stories:**
- [ ] **G2-S4 See my distance month by month.** As a member, I want to see my total for each past month, so that I can compare months and see whether I am keeping it up.
  - Acceptance:
    - "My distance" lists every month in which I logged at least one run, newest first, with its total. For example: "September 2026: 64.0 km".
    - Each month's total equals the sum of that month's logged runs after any edits or deletions.
  - Depends on: G2-S1. INVEST: all pass.

### Dependency order (stub 2)
1. G2-S1 (depends on G1-S1 in stub 1)
2. G2-S2, G2-S3, G2-S4 (each depends on G2-S1 only)

**Thinnest end-to-end path:** G2-S1 (log and see the month's total), then G2-S3.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity

All of these await the owner's review. Each one says what it affects.

1. **Two goals, split along the vision's own sentence.** Run leaders sit inside Goal 1, with no goal of their own. *(Goal structure)*
2. **"An attendance count" is read as a record of which members came, and the count is derived from it.** SC2 (attendees who signed up beforehand) and SC4 (active members are those who came) cannot be computed from a headcount alone. *(G1-S6)*
3. **The run leader is whoever posts the run,** as the vision defines it. Any signed-in member may post. There is no separate leader role and no admin. Only the poster can edit, cancel or record attendance for a run. *(G1-S1, G1-S2, G1-S6)*
4. **Sign-in uses an email sign-in link, starting from the club's chat link.** The first sign-in creates the member (email and name), and the member stays signed in on that phone. Anyone with the link can join; there is no check against a member list. Alternatives: a club invite code, or members approved by an organiser. *(G1-S1)*
5. **Everything, including the run list, needs sign-in.** Today the schedule lives in the members-only chat, so it is not made public. Because sign-in persists, SC1's path is still just "tap the link, see the list". *(G1-S1, G1-S4)*
6. **Opened from a link on the phone, with no app-store install.** Members are on their phones in the chat, and an install step works against SC1, SC3 and adoption. This is a constraint on the product; the technology choice is left to implementation planning. *(both stubs)*
7. **"This week" means the next 7 days counted from today, not the calendar week Monday to Sunday.** On a Sunday a calendar week would show only that Sunday. Runs whose start time has passed drop off the list. *(G1-S4)*
8. **Sign-up closes at the start time, and each sign-up keeps the time it was made.** "Beforehand" means before the start time. *(G1-S5)*
9. **Attendance counts members only.** Guests who are not members are not recorded, because the criteria and the audience are about members. *(G1-S6)*
10. **Distances are in kilometres only.** The date defaults to today. Future dates are refused. Past dates are allowed and count towards the month they fall in. *(G2-S1)*
11. **A month is a calendar month in the club's time zone** (the club is in one city). *(G2-S1, G2-S3, G2-S4)*
12. **Logged runs are private to the member, and there is no leaderboard.** The vision says "their own monthly distance". *(G2-S1)*
13. **There is no in-app report of SC2 or SC4.** The stored data (sign-up times, attendance per member, logged runs) lets both be computed with a query. *(G1-S5, G1-S6, G2-S1)*
14. **The shared sign-in lives in G1-S1,** because Goal 1 uses it most: posting, sign-up and attendance. If the owner builds Goal 2 first, sign-in moves into G2-S1, the cross-goal dependency reverses, and nothing else changes. *(G1-S1, G2-S1, stub depends_on)*
15. **No delivery phases.** The agent's method would group stories into "Walking Skeleton / Flesh out / Polish" phases. That grouping was left out because scheduling is the owner's call. *(whole decomposition)*
16. **The readiness gate was checked by hand** against the documented checks, because the library could not be read or run from here. *(gate)*

## Open questions for the owner

1. **Goals:** are the two goals right? (In an interactive run this would be the goal-validation question. Decision 1 is the default for now.)
2. **Delivery strategy:** build the thinnest end-to-end path first, go goal by goal, or go actor by actor? This is the owner's call. Recommendation, nothing more: build the thinnest path in both goals first (G1-S1, G1-S5, G1-S6, G2-S1, G2-S3), because SC2 and SC4 can only be measured once sign-up, attendance and logging all exist.
3. **Stand-in leaders:** may another member record attendance when the poster cannot lead the run? (Decision 3 currently says no.)
4. **Who may join:** anyone with the link, or only people on a club member list? (Decision 4)
5. **Guests:** should guests who are not members be counted? (Decision 9)
6. **A club-wide view of the SC2 and SC4 numbers:** wanted? The vision names no organiser role that would use it. (Decision 13)
7. **Miles:** needed for anyone? (Decision 10)

## Stories considered but not included

These are listed in full so the owner can add any of them.

- **"Log a group run I attended in one tap."** After the run leader records me as present, the app offers to log that run with the date filled in. The distance could be filled in too if posts gain a distance field. This supports SC4 directly. It was left out for two reasons: the vision's scope gives posts no distance, and it would add a second dependency between the goals. If added: depends on G1-S6 and G2-S1, longest chain 3, so it fits.
- **Reminders to sign up or to log a run.** The vision's scope does not mention notifications, but does not exclude them either. They would serve SC2 and SC4.
- **Seeing the names of who else is going.** Not in the scope's wording ("sign-up"), but it could make members more likely to sign up (SC2). If added: depends on G1-S5, longest chain 3.
- **This month's distance shown on the run-list screen,** so one screen serves both halves of the vision. If added: depends on G1-S4 and G2-S1, which is a second dependency between the goals.
